name: Familial Pterygium of the Conjunctiva

criteria.description: Positive family history of conjunctival pterygium in first-degree relatives
Presence of bilateral conjunctival pterygium with characteristic fibrovascular growth
Lack of significant environmental risk factors such as UV exposure or chronic irritation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral conjunctival pterygium with positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by family history; genetic testing is not routinely available.

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing fibrovascular conjunctival growth extending onto corneal surface
genetic: Familial aggregation suggests autosomal dominant inheritance pattern; specific gene mutations not identified
other: Clinical observation of characteristic triangular conjunctival lesion with vascularization

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with UV exposure and environmental risk factors
Later onset compared to familial form
Irregular, nodular lesion with possible ulceration

redFlags: Unilateral lesion with irregular borders or pigmentation
Significant visual loss or corneal ulceration
references: Orphanet: Familial Pterygium of the Conjunctiva, ORPHA:2989
Kanski JJ, Bowling B. Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach. 8th Edition. Elsevier; 2015.
Dushku N, Reid TW. Pterygium pathogenesis: corneal invasion by matrix metalloproteinase expressing altered limbal epithelial basal cells. Arch Ophthalmol. 1994.
